brief: The Ācārya tiptoeing into the library with a lamp and bowing gravely to Śuka who has puffed himself up on a shelf; Dādī suppressing a laugh; the ink-stained blue-black spirit waving its pen at the next shelf.
The round spice seller with arms folded firing questions at the small yellow spirit, who shrinks behind your leg; Dādī holding up four fingers; Śuka cocking his head; spice heaps in the foreground.

The spice seller sitting behind his stall with a very old green-lidded wooden chest at his feet, shaking his head with a smile; the small yellow spirit hovering above the lid; you and Dādī looking at it with curiosity.

A riverside market under striped awnings: baskets of fruit, heaps of red and yellow spice, swinging brass scales; a small saffron-yellow spirit darting between stalls pointing at things, a round cheerful spice seller watching him, you, Dādī and Śuka among the shoppers.
The small saffron-yellow spirit tugging at your sleeve and pointing between the spice stall, the river and a grove of trees beyond the market; Dādī smiling; Śuka looking where he points.

The Ācārya's small, lamplit house behind the school: a low desk with a palm-leaf book, a reed pen, a folded saffron shawl and a string of beads; a slim warm-gold spirit holding a tiny lamp touching each thing softly; you and Dādī sitting on the floor mat.
The ghat crowded with many boats pulling up to the steps, each with its boatman calling out, a small grey-blue spirit cupping his hands as if announcing them; Dādī and Śuka watching from the steps.

Two tall white herons standing side by side on one leg each in the shallows of the river at the ghat, perfectly mirrored in the water; Śuka on Dādī's shoulder counting on his claw; boats beginning to gather behind.
